Note that some of the plan pages linked below say their plans were "repealed by the Township of Langley on June 15, 2026" and replaced by Bylaw 6202 or 6203, but the Township's own Willoughby Community Plan Update page shows only first and second reading of Bylaws 6201, 6202 and 6203 on May 25, 2026, with a public hearing set for June 15, 2026. items.t: The page's scope: browser title "Township of Langley Land Use Plans, OCP Maps & Zoning Updates," covering the whole Township of Langley through twelve plan tiles — Aldergrove, Brookswood-Fernridge, Carvolth, Central Gordon Estate, Jericho, Latimer, Murrayville, North East Gordon Estate, Routley, Smith, Walnut Grove, Williams, Yorkson — each summarizing a community or neighbourhood plan and linking to tol.ca.
On MLS®, there's no single area for this topic; this page covers the whole Township.

Where condos are planned: the Township's Willoughby update treats Willoughby as its urban growth area, expected to take a large share of future population growth, with TransLink's proposed bus rapid transit on 200 Street as a key driver and a new transit-oriented development permit area proposed. That's plan policy, not buildings.

Planning structure, in the Township's own description: Township community planning is guided by the Sustainability Charter, and "The Official Community Plan and component Community and Neighbourhood Plans help make the vision a reality by providing policies and actions specific to each area"; the Community and Policy Planning division also owns functional plans including the Agricultural Viability Strategy, Climate Action Strategy, Heritage Strategy and Fraser Highway Employment Lands Area Plan.

One plan-level school fact is recorded in the Township's Gordon Neighbourhood Plan draft: Bylaw No. 6203's plan area includes Langley Fire Hall No. 4 and a daycare and learning centre among its key institutional uses — a draft-plan statement, with the bylaw itself at reading stage only.

items.t: The December 2025 update set included the Aldergrove, Murrayville, Fort Langley, Walnut Grove and Northwest Langley community plans and the Yorkson, Smith and Williams Neighbourhood Plans.

The Willoughby Community Plan started as Bylaw 1836 (1979) and is now part of Bylaw 6200 (adopted December 1, 2025). The Township's 2026 update proposes a new Willoughby Community Plan (Bylaw No. 6201), a Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan (Bylaw No. 6202, combining the Carvolth, Latimer, Jericho, Routley and Southwest Gordon Estate plans) and a Gordon Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6203, combining the Central and Northeast Gordon Estate plans), plus a new development permit area for transit-oriented development. Check the current status of these with the Township.

Murrayville Community Plan (verified at bylaw level): Bylaw 1988 No. 2661, adopted April 17, 1989 as an amendment to the Langley Official Community Plan Bylaw 1979 No. 1842, since amended including by the 2025 OCP Update (Bylaw No. 6200, December 1, 2025); the plan describes Murrayville on both sides of the Fraser Highway immediately east of the City of Langley.

Zoning in the Township is under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500. Small-scale housing (Bylaw No. 6020, adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units on eligible lots of 280 m² or less and 4 on lots from 280 m² to 4,050 m², with no 6-unit option, and since April 27, 2026 a development permit area sets design guidelines for it. To be eligible, a lot must be inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on city water and sewer, not heritage-designated, not in a transit-oriented area and no larger than 4,050 m². Suites are capped at 120 m². The Township's one transit-oriented area is on 196 Street in Willowbrook, around the proposed Surrey–Langley SkyTrain station; designated by the Province on May 2, 2025, it allows minimum densities of 8 to 20 storeys within 800 m, depending on distance from the station.

items.t: The Gordon plan area's boundaries are in the draft, even though the bylaw is not adopted. Bylaw No. 6203's draft plan places the Gordon neighbourhood in southeast Willoughby, bounded by 73A and 72 Avenues and north of Crush Crescent to the ALR boundary, the Willowbrook Connector and ALR boundary to the east, 68 and 66A Avenues to the south, and 206 and 202B Street to the west — useful for identifying whether a parcel is even in the draft area, without treating the draft as law.

Brookswood-Fernridge is still being refined lot-by-lot. The Rinn Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6010, adopted June 10, 2024) already has a Rinn Update 2026 (Bylaw No. 6219) recorded May 25, 2026 — in this area the neighbourhood plan, not just the community plan, is the document to check before pricing a parcel.

The December 2025 update already changed more than the tiles suggest. The Bylaw No. 6200 update set (adopted December 1, 2025) included not only the OCP but the Aldergrove, Murrayville, Fort Langley, Walnut Grove and Northwest Langley community plans and the Yorkson, Smith and Williams neighbourhood plans — a parcel in any of those areas is under a December 2025 plan version even if its tile looks unchanged.

Two municipalities named Langley share one market row. The SnapStats Langley community figures in combine the Township and the City of Langley — a Township parcel's plan position cannot be read off a combined City-plus-Township median, and the City's bylaws are a separate check from everything in.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Township of Langley Plans

items.t: This page lists the Township's community plans (Aldergrove, Brookswood-Fernridge, Murrayville, Walnut Grove and Willoughby) and the Willoughby neighbourhood plans (Carvolth, Central Gordon Estate, Jericho, Latimer, North East Gordon Estate, Routley, Smith, Williams and Yorkson), each linking to the Township's website.

A Township property can be covered by several layers: the Official Community Plan (updated by Bylaw No. 6200 on December 1, 2025), a community plan, a neighbourhood plan where there is one, Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (including small-scale housing Bylaw No. 6020), and development permit areas such as the one for small-scale housing adopted April 27, 2026. A plan designation is policy; it doesn't mean serviced lots or land for sale.

Two key plans: the Murrayville Community Plan (Bylaw No. 2661), adopted April 17, 1989 and since updated, including by the 2025 OCP update (Bylaw No. 6200); and the Rinn Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6010), part of the Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan (Bylaw No. 5300), adopted June 10, 2024, with a 2026 update (Bylaw No. 6219) introduced May 25, 2026.

6201 (Willoughby Community Plan), 6202 (Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan) and 6203 (Gordon Neighbourhood Plan) received first and second reading on May 25, 2026 only, with a Public Hearing directed for June 15, 2026 — proposals at reading stage, not adopted law and not land inventory.

Transit: TransLink's proposed bus rapid transit on 200 Street is a key driver of the Township's Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Township of Langley Plans

items.t: The Township's 2025 OCP update (Bylaw No. 6200) was adopted December 1, 2025, and included the Aldergrove, Murrayville, Fort Langley, Walnut Grove and Northwest Langley community plans and the Yorkson, Smith and Williams neighbourhood plans. The Willoughby Community Plan (originally Bylaw 1836) is now part of Bylaw 6200. Its proposed update (Bylaws 6201–6203) had first and second reading on May 25, 2026, with a public hearing set for June 15, 2026, and isn't adopted yet.

Agricultural Land Reserve rules (for Township properties in the ALR): subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR homes can't be stratified. The main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is only allowed inside it, and one additional home can be up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones. Farm tax status has three income tiers: $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha, and $10,000 under 0.8 ha, with applications due by October 31.

items.t: June 15, 2026 was a hearing date, not a repeal date (Township record, read Nov 1, 2026). The Township's Willoughby update page records first and second reading of Bylaw Nos. 6201, 6202 and 6203 on May 25, 2026 and a Public Hearing directed for June 15, 2026.
The Murrayville plan is from 1989 and still live. Bylaw No. 2661 (adopted April 17, 1989) as amended by the 2025 OCP Update — read the current consolidated version, not the 1989 text alone.

Rinn is still being refined lot by lot. The Rinn Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6010, adopted June 10, 2024) already has a Rinn Update 2026 (Bylaw No. 6219) recorded May 25, 2026 — in Brookswood-Fernridge the neighbourhood plan, not just the community plan, drives a parcel.

faq.a: 6202/6203, but the Township's Willoughby update page records only first and second reading of Bylaw Nos. 6201, 6202 and 6203 on May 25, 2026, with a Public Hearing directed for June 15, 2026 — June 15, 2026 is the hearing date in the Township record, not a recorded repeal date. Confirm adoption with the Township before relying on either version.
faq.q: Have the Carvolth, Jericho, Latimer, Routley and Gordon Estate plans been repealed?

faq.a: In this order: the OCP designation (updated by Bylaw No. 6200, December 1, 2025), then the community plan, then any neighbourhood plan, then the current zoning under Bylaw No. 2500. The plans show where the Township wants growth; the zoning shows what can be built today without a rezoning.
faq.q: How do I read a Township parcel before offering?

faq.a: A community plan originating as Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (adopted December 1, 2025), with a 2026 update package (Bylaws 6201–6203) at first/second reading as of May 25, 2026.
faq.q: What is the Willoughby plan, in one line?

faq.a: Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (adopted December 1, 2025).
faq.q: Which bylaw is the Willoughby Community Plan?

faq.a: In this order: the OCP designation (updated by Bylaw No. 6200, December 1, 2025), then the community plan, then any neighbourhood plan, then the current zoning under Bylaw No. 2500. The plans show where the Township wants growth; the zoning shows what can be built today without a rezoning.

faq.a: No — designation is policy. Subdivision needs Approving Officer approval, and servicing is governed by the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw 2019 No. 5382; ALR parcels also need ALC approval to subdivide.
faq.q: Does a plan designation mean I can subdivide?

faq.a: The Township's long-range policy plan, given effect through the Langley Official Community Plan Bylaw 1979 No. 1842 as amended — most recently by the 2025 OCP Update, Bylaw No. 6200, adopted December 1, 2025 — with component Community and Neighbourhood Plans providing area-specific policies under it
faq.q: What is the Township of Langley's Official Community Plan?

faq.a: The plans set area policy while the zoning amendments do the permitting: Bylaw No. 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units at ≤280 m² and 4 units at 280–4,050 m² on eligible lots, and an OCP Schedule 4 Development Permit Area for SSMUH form and character was adopted April 27, 2026
